annotations.variable_note: On average, before fiscal year 2014, federal Medicaid payments represented approximately 57 percent of total Medicaid payments. The ACA, which expanded Medicaid coverage starting in 2014, provides enhanced federal matching rates for services to those made eligible by that act, leading to a federal share for all Medicaid of about 65 percent, on average. In addition, for the duration of the coronavirus public health emergency, the Families First Coronavirus Relief Act increased matching rates by 6.2 percentage points for services provided to people who were not made eligible by the ACA. The American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 increased the federal medical assistance percentage by 10 percentage points for certain Medicaid home- and community-based services from April 1, 2021, through March 31, 2022, provided that states use the enhanced funding to improve those services. In total, CBO estimates, the average federal matching rate for Medicaid in 2021 and 2022 will be about 67 percent.
